presentation.name: Yvan SANSON
presentation.text: I move comfortably across the stack, including TypeScript, Go, Python, and Java, and have hands-on DevOps experience with Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD on AWS and GCP. Outside of work, I dig into systems programming and mobile development through personal projects: a BitTorrent client in Rust, a tree-walking interpreter in Go, and a SwiftUI app for tracking bike maintenance, because I like understanding how the tools I rely on actually work under the hood.

overview.title: Corpy & Co
overview.intro: Corpy & Co. builds AI quality management software for regulated and quality-critical industries — manufacturing, medical devices, and beyond. Since January 2024, I've worked as a full-stack engineer on Confide, Corpy's flagship product suite, alongside R&D, infrastructure, and QA work. Here's a closer look at the two applications I contribute to the most.

mlops.name: Confide MLOps
mlops.tagline: One platform for the whole AI lifecycle.
mlops.blurb: An MLOps and AI quality management platform covering the full lifecycle: data management, annotation, model training, and production operations — built for industries where model decisions need to be explainable and auditable.

cms.name: Confide CMS
cms.blurb: Confide's content and configuration management application. Details coming soon.

mlops.title: Confide MLOps
mlops.tagline: One platform for the whole AI lifecycle.
mlops.intro: Confide is Corpy & Co.'s MLOps and AI quality management platform — one place to take a model from raw data through training, evaluation, and operations, with QA and explainability built in rather than bolted on.
mlops.gapTitle: Shipping a model is easy. Operating one you can trust isn't.
mlops.gap: Most ML work dies in the gap between a notebook and production: data scattered across folders, transforms nobody can reproduce, models with no record of what they were trained on. Confide closes that gap by running the whole lifecycle — data, training, evaluation, operations — through one platform where everything is versioned and traceable.
mlops.deploymentNote: Because it serves quality-critical industries, deployment isn't just the cloud: releases ship the same way to internal staging and production, and to offline client machines with no direct network access.

data.label: Data Management
data.description: Assets are uploaded, versioned, and tagged into annotation sets — a browsable, searchable dataset instead of loose folders. A set can evolve, with new batches added or bad images pruned, without ever losing track of what a given model was trained on.

annotation.label: Annotation
annotation.description: An embedded Label Studio editor handles manual work, bounding boxes, polygons, and class tags included. For bulk coverage, prompt-based auto-annotation takes a text description of what to detect and runs a model across the whole dataset with a confidence threshold, turning labeling from per-image work into a supervised batch job.

analysis.label: Analysis
analysis.description: Before any training starts, exploratory data analysis scores a dataset on completeness, consistency, and accuracy, with a clustering view and AI-generated insights that read the plots for you — well-separated clusters, balanced classes, and what that means for the model about to be trained.

training.label: Model Training & Evaluation
training.description: Training runs are versioned and tied back to the exact data that produced them. Results come back as confusion matrices, confidence distributions, per-class precision-recall curves, and a blunt best-and-worst class ranking, with evaluation and explainability runs one click away from the same screen.

operations.label: Operations
operations.description: A trained model is packaged into a versioned container image — the same release unit whether it ships to staging, production, or a fully offline client machine. Operations screens track which version is live where, next to the metrics and explainability output for that release.

dm.name: Data Management
dm.description: Manages, analyzes, and processes data — exploratory analysis, preprocessing, and versioned pipelines that keep the lineage of every transform.

mm.name: Model Management
mm.description: Manages, trains, and evaluates models, so every version carries a traceable history of what it was trained on and how it scored.

xai.name: Explainability
xai.description: Explainable-AI tooling built into operations, because in quality-critical deployments, “the model said so” isn't an answer.

autoAnnotation.title: Prompt-based auto-annotation
autoAnnotation.description: Describing a class in plain text is enough — a detection model runs it across the whole dataset with a confidence threshold, and everything above that threshold is queued for human review instead of being written straight to the dataset.

anomalyGeneration.title: Anomaly generation
anomalyGeneration.description: Factories produce thousands of good parts and almost no defective ones, which starves anomaly detection of training data. This tool composites real defect patches onto normal images with Poisson blending — position, size, brightness, and blend strength are all tunable — turning a handful of real defects into a usable training set.

explainability.title: Explainability (XAI)
explainability.description: Explainability tooling sits next to evaluation metrics in the operations screens, one click from any training result, because in regulated industries a model's decision needs a defensible reason, not just a confidence score.

control.title: Control plane
control.description: The web and API layer registers each module and holds the metadata records for the whole platform.

execution.title: Execution plane
execution.description: Long-running work never blocks a request: pipeline runs, training, and evaluation execute on a fleet of asynchronous workers.

artifacts.title: Artifacts
artifacts.description: Everything that crosses an environment boundary is an artifact — versioned container images in a registry, pipeline configs in the database, and lineage logs tying every model version back to its dataset snapshot and deployment event.

pipelines.title: Pipelines are versioned database objects
pipelines.description: A preprocessing pipeline isn't a script someone ran once — it's a config stored in the database with a version, a parent it can inherit from, and the dataset it belongs to. That makes every run re-runnable and answers the lineage question: which transforms, in which version, produced this data.

modularCore.title: One AI core, installable in pieces
modularCore.description: The AI core is modularized into an installable package with optional add-ons per module, so a deployment only installs what it needs. Missing features degrade to “feature disabled” instead of a crash, and client installs stay small because they only carry the modules they use.

releaseUnit.title: The release unit is an image, not source code
releaseUnit.description: A passing build produces a versioned container image pushed to a registry; staging and production run containers only, with no source code on the box. For offline client machines, the same images travel as saved archives and load without touching the internet.

smallestMachine.title: Designed for the smallest machine, not the biggest
smallestMachine.description: Realistic datasets used to kill pipeline workers on 16GB machines — images loaded eagerly into memory, transforms piling up in lists. The fix was architectural: pass paths instead of arrays, load lazily inside transforms, stream per asset, and write to temp files. Client hardware is a constraint, not an afterthought.

contribution.title: My Contribution
contribution.intro: I work on Confide MLOps as a full-stack engineer, moving between the frontend, backend, and the infrastructure that ships it.
highlights: I built the licensing system that ties activation to cryptographic hardware fingerprints and validates over-the-air, covering both cloud and fully offline deployments.
I own the CI/CD pipeline for the platform, which cut deployment time significantly and gave the sales team a clearer way to demo builds to prospects.
I helped build an image inference pipeline targeting sub-20ms inference and response time, for near real-time quality checks on production lines.
I created a custom installer for offline deployments, so the platform can be set up entirely inside a client's own network with no external dependency.
